sources.title: 'No nation left behind' says Burnham after meeting first ministers in Glasgow
Local devolution decisions rest solely with Scotland and Wales, first ministers tell Burnham
First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

en.title: UK First Ministers Meet in Glasgow to Discuss Devolution Powers
en.dek: Prime Minister Andy Burnham met Scottish and Welsh first ministers in Glasgow to discuss deeper devolution and regional powers.
facts: Andy Burnham met first ministers John Swinney and Rhun ap Iorwerth in Glasgow on 30 October 2026.
John Swinney said devolution decisions rest solely with Holyrood.
Rhun ap Iorwerth said the meeting was a step forward for Wales.
The Guardian reported that the first ministers told Burnham that local devolution decisions rest with their parliaments.
body: On 30 October 2026, Andy Burnham met first ministers John Swinney and Rhun ap Iorwerth in Glasgow. He said he wanted to ensure no nation was left behind and urged that Scotland and Wales decide how to implement deeper devolution. He also said the UK government would look at arrangements for further devolution of employment support for young people.

John Swinney said devolution decisions rest solely with Holyrood and added that he would work constructively and collaboratively with Burnham. He also said Burnham would not bypass the Scottish parliament. Swinney welcomed the recognition that Westminster is not working for Scotland.

Rhun ap Iorwerth said the meeting was a step forward for Wales and that the UK government would consider loosening financial restrictions. He also said the Welsh government would decide how and when to use its reserves. Burnham said the meeting was positive.

The Guardian reported that the first ministers told Burnham that local devolution decisions rest with their parliaments and that the UK government described the talks as constructive. It mentioned that defence secretary Wes Streeting had criticised Swinney's government before the summit. It noted that Michelle O'Neill did not attend the talks.

BBC reported that the meeting followed rows between the Welsh and UK government over the chancellor's budget, which ap Iorwerth had said was not serious about Wales. It also said the Welsh government had a real‑terms cut in funding. It said the meeting was described as constructive by Downing Street.
en.context: The meeting followed the UK budget, which the Welsh government said left a real‑terms cut in funding. The discussion focused on devolving more powers for employment support, reindustrialisation, and financial flexibility. The UK government aims to move all four nations at the same pace on devolution.
en.imageCaption: Andy Burnham met the first ministers from Scotland and Wales and representatives from Northern Ireland in Glasgow
